primary_diagnosis_treated: Uncontrolled essential hypertension leading to hypertensive nephrosclerosis (CKD stage 4)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG136 (Hypertension) and NICE NG203/TA775 (Chronic kidney disease and SGLT2 inhibitors)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg then 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Titrate to target dose over 8‑12 weeks, then lifelong – review annually
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade for blood pressure control and renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NG136 first‑line ACE‑I for hypertension; NG203 ACE‑I recommended for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong – repeat lipid panel in 6 weeks, then review annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD and treatment of severe dyslipidaemia
medications.nice_justification: NG136/NG203 recommend high‑intensity statin for all CKD patients and for heterozygous FH

medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor eGFR and renal outcomes every 3 months
medications.purpose: Renoprotective therapy to slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: TA775 recommends dapagliflozin for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² irrespective of diabetes status

medications.duration: Current medication – to be discontinued and replaced with atorvastatin
medications.purpose: Existing lipid‑lowering therapy (insufficient intensity per guideline)
medications.nice_justification: Guideline recommends a statin, but dose/intensity is below recommended high‑intensity regimen

medications.dose: One tablet as needed for breakthrough pain
medications.duration: As required – review pain regimen at next visit
medications.nice_justification: No specific NICE recommendation; continued for symptom control

medications.duration: As required – review pain regimen at next visit
medications.purpose: Baseline control of chronic neck and low‑back pain
medications.nice_justification: No specific NICE recommendation; continued for symptom control

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined use increases risk of statin‑induced myopathy due to additive CYP3A4 inhibition
Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: If amlodipine is required, consider reducing atorvastatin to 20 mg or use pravastatin/rosuvastatin

contraindications.reason: eGFR not yet confirmed ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²; contraindicated below this threshold
contraindications.alternative: Hold dapagliflozin until eGFR is measured and confirmed ≥20

contraindications.reason: Pregnancy status unknown – ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy
contraindications.alternative: If patient is pregnant, switch to an ARB only after confirming safety (or avoid RAAS blockade until postpartum)

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – required to confirm eligibility for ACE‑I dosing and SGLT2 inhibitor; assume eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m² for planning but order urgent eGFR.
Serum potassium not provided – needed before initiating ACE‑I/ARB; assume K⁺ ≤4.5 mmol/L and obtain baseline.
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not available – needed to confirm proteinuria for CKD management.
Patient age not supplied – ACE‑I preferred if <55 y; CCB preferred if ≥55 y. Chosen ACE‑I for renal protection regardless of age.
Pregnancy status not documented – ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy; verify before prescribing.
Liver function tests not provided – required before high‑intensity atorvastatin; assume normal but order LFTs.
Diabetes status unknown – SGLT2 inhibitor benefit independent of diabetes but confirm HbA1c.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily and titrate to 10 mg for hypertension and renal protection (NG136, NG203). Replace low‑intensity simvastatin with high‑intensity atorvastatin 40 mg daily for cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD and severe dyslipidaemia (NG136/NG203). Consider dapagliflozin 10 mg daily once eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m² is confirmed (TA775). Continue current opioid analgesics with regular review. Order urgent labs (eGFR, potassium, ACR, LFTs, HbA1c) and refer to nephrology for CKD stage 4 management. Provide lifestyle advice (salt restriction, weight loss, exercise, smoking cessation).
